content.description: Diagram showing SST (Special Service Tool) connected to fuel system with pressure gauge

items: Install a gasket, SST, another gasket and union bolt to the delivery pipe as shown in the figure.
Wipe off any splattered gasoline.
Reconnect the battery cable.

content.description: Diagram showing fuel pump and pressure check connector location

items: Short both terminals of the fuel pump check connector.
Turn on the ignition switch.
Measure the fuel pressure.

content.text: If high pressure, replace the pressure regulator. If low pressure, check the following parts.

items: Fuel hoses and connection
Fuel pump
Fuel filter
Pressure regulator

content.description: Diagram showing disconnection of vacuum sensing hose from pressure regulator

items: Disconnect the service wire from the service connector.
Start the engine.
Disconnect the vacuum sensing hose from the pressure regulator and plug.
Measure the fuel pressure at idling.
Reconnect the vacuum sensing hose to the pressure regulator.

content.description: Diagram showing reconnection of vacuum sensing hose to pressure regulator

items: Measure the fuel pressure at idling.

content.text: If not pressure, check the vacuum sensing hose and pressure regulator.

items: Stop the engine. Check that the fuel pressure remains above 1.5 kg/cm² (21 psi, 147 kPa) for 5 minutes after the engine is turned off.

content.text: If not within specification, check the fuel pump, pressure regulator and/or injectors.

items: After checking fuel pressure, disconnect the battery ground cable and carefully remove the SST to prevent gasoline from splashing.
Using new gaskets, reconnect the cold start injector hose to the delivery pipe.
Connect the wiring connector to the cold start injector.
Check for fuel leakage.
